name: Bauhaus modern tableware
summary: Plain white porcelain made for a factory, in simple solid forms. The designers drop the ornament and the gold, and shape a service that stacks, pours well and costs little to make.

philosophy.core_thesis: A service is a tool for the table: it is a few simple solids, in white, that fit one another and give good use.
design_principles: Build each piece from a few simple solids: a cylinder, a sphere, a flat disc.
Keep the surface white and undecorated, and let the glaze and the form carry the look.
Make the pieces stack and nest, so that a service takes little room in a cupboard.
Set the handle and the spout by use: the hand fits the handle, and the lip does not drip.
Reduce the service to 20 to 30 shapes that serve all meals.
Cast the piece in a mould so that each one is the same as the next.
Print or band only a single thin line in a colour when the buyer asks for it.
anti_patterns: A gilt rim with scrolls and flowers
A modelled relief of leaves and shells
A hand-painted floral pattern in many colours
A thick, hand-thrown wall with a visible tool mark

form.shape: Flat plates with a narrow rim, straight-sided bowls, cylinder tureens, and stacking sauceboats and egg cups.
form.profile: A flat floor and a short, straight rim; each piece is a simple solid with a sharp, clean edge.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat base with a small foot ring or no ring; the rim is a plain edge about 10 mm wide.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 20 to 26 cm and wall 2.5 to 3.5 mm thick; the height of a bowl equals half its width.
rules: Use one outline for the whole service, in circle and straight line.
Make the pieces nest and stack in columns.
Keep the rim plain and narrow, with no moulded border.

bodies.rule: Use a hard-paste porcelain that casts well and fires white and dense. Do not use earthenware: the service has to be hard and thin.

forming.joins: Handles and spouts are cast with the body or luted with slip, and fettled to a clean line.
forming.details: A clean mould seam that the worker removes, a plain maker mark in the base, and an even white glaze.

glaze.pattern: No pattern; at most a thin line or band in one colour on the rim.
glaze.gloss: Bright to satin gloss, about 70 to 90 GU, on a pure white ground.
glaze.wear: The glaze stays hard and shows a fine mark of cutlery; there is no gold or enamel to wear.

palette.strategy: White first, with a single thin line in grey, black or a primary colour when the buyer asks for it.

firing.kiln: A gas- or coal-fired tunnel kiln with saggars; a biscuit firing and a glaze firing at high heat.
processes: glaze firing at about 1400 °C in reduction
firing.scale: A state factory that made services by the tens of thousands, from one set of master moulds.
firing.signs: A faint mould seam, a factory mark in the base, and the same white on every piece.

pieces.form: Flat plate with a narrow plain rim, in a stacking series of 4 sizes
Shallow bowl with a straight, narrow rim
Cylinder tureen with a flat lid and a ball knop
Stacking boat with a clean lip that does not drip
Plain cup on a short foot, in a stacking series

positive: stacking plates with a narrow rim
cylinder tureen with a ball knop
studio product photograph, soft grey ground

evidence.title: Theodor Bogler teapot, Model 545, 1923, Bauhaus Museum Weimar

emotion.target_response: A clear, calm order: the viewer sees a plain white set that does its job, and feels that nothing is added and nothing is missing.

use_cases: a museum label on 1930s German porcelain
avoid_when: the brief wants ornament, gold or painting
the brief wants a hand-made look

modifiers.how: Keep the plain form, change to a stoneware or an earthenware with a satin or matt glaze, and soften the edge.
Replace the straight edge with a soft curve and add a muted colour glaze.
Add painted bands in flat colour and sharp angles to the white ground.

wall_thickness.note: Thin and even; the wall is as thin as the casting allows.
